overall_reason: One UI sans (Segoe UI drawn at 1440, from a -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI" stack; system-ui at 375) sets every role, which fits a product component in Operate mode, so TYP-005 does not apply. Every label is set in capitals and tracked: the head 'RECENT DEPLOYS' (12px, 0.12em), the button 'DEPLOY', the meta 'MAIN · MAYA CHEN' and the times 'JUST NOW', '12M AGO', '1H AGO' (10px, 0.08em), with a tracked line 'PRODUCTION · 3 DEPLOYS' under the head.

score.reason: T-LABEL-TRANSFORM fails on 7 tracked caps labels (TYP-015), including a person's name and relative times that read worse in caps; T-LADDER and T-LEADING otherwise pass.

findings.title: Small labels earn their caps
findings.evidence: The type table counts 7 small caps or tracked labels, for example 'RECENT DEPLOYS' at 12px with 0.12em, 'MAIN · MAYA CHEN' at 10px with 0.08em and '12M AGO' at 10px with 0.08em (01-evidence/tiles/1440-00.png). The capitals are in the text itself (text-transform: none). The line 'PRODUCTION · 3 DEPLOYS' is an eyebrow and stays with the sweep (SLP-001).
findings.before: Head, button, meta and times in tracked capitals at 10 to 12px
findings.after: Sentence case, untracked, in the body face a step smaller: 'Recent deploys', 'main · Maya Chen', '12m ago'
findings.why: Removing the caps makes every label easier to read: '12M AGO' can read as twelve months, and a person's name in capitals loses its word shape.
findings.root: label style (uppercase text with 0.08 to 0.14em tracking)

strengths: Row names stay in sentence case at 14px/500, the one role the caps style leaves alone.
